newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp-American Express rumors revived on Street.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp-American Express rumors revived on Street.

text.p: Chistmas Eve rumors that merger talks between American Express Co and Citicorp had been revived were greeted with skepticism by arbitragers.
"I personally think it is preposterous," said one arbitrager, who did not want to be identified.
A spokesman for Citicorp declined comment on the matter, citing a policy of not responding to market rumors or speculation.
An American Express spokesman also declined comment but reiterated a statement issued over a week ago that the company is not now engaged in any merger negotiatons.

"I have heard nothing about it, but it is not a deal people should get excited about," said another arbitrager, also asking anonymity. "It (a merger) would be very dilutive to Citicorp's earnings. I don't see American Express selling for less than $65 or $70 per share.
"At $65, it is a $32 billion deal, and at $70 it is a $36 billion deal. I just don't see it."
American Express closed up 2-3/4 at 59-5/8 in Tuesday's abbreviated Christmas Eve trading. Citicorp rose 1-3/8 to 105-1/4.
Earlier this month, published reports said the two companies had held unsuccessful merger talks. The reports were never confirmed.
